attribution_v2.definition: hard-infeasible(step) := minimum total CBF relaxation required at that step > 1e-3 m (1 mm). The relaxation is obtained from an ALWAYS-FEASIBLE QP that minimises total slack, so the verdict never depends on a solver status flag.
attribution_v2.why_changed: The previous zero-slack test used prob.status in ('optimal','optimal_inaccurate') and reported 391 infeasible cells. The 23 additional cells found here carry relaxations of 2.3e-2 to 2.60e+1 m (8 of them > 10 m), i.e. they were ECOS false negatives under 'optimal_inaccurate', not boundary jitter. 391 is wrong; 414 is correct.

oracle_v2.note: oracle_slack_at_cpa is the ORACLE-REPLAY QP's relaxation slack, not Stage-2's. The text's '20 of the 22' refers to this quantity.

wind_eta_calibration.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-04 (blocking #1 from round 1, never closed until now)
wind_eta_calibration.finding: The canonical pipeline runs at eta_w=0.3 with gust_std=3.0 (product 0.9). eval_common.py:116 constructs UrbanWindField(eta_w=WIND_ETA) WITHOUT passing gust_std, so it silently takes the wind.py default of 3.0. The manuscript declared a nominal of 0.5 (product 1.5). These are NOT the same disturbance: measured at seed 7 over 64 positions, gust RMS is 0.6654 vs 1.1090, max|gust| 2.0343 vs 3.3904, max abs difference 1.356 m/s, amplitude ratio exactly 0.6 = 0.3/0.5.
wind_eta_calibration.adjudication: Route A: the CODE is authoritative, the manuscript declaration was an isolated typo. Every result in the paper (7-arm table, Stage-1b ADE 1.839 matching the stated 1.84, fig02, fig05) reproduces byte-for-byte at 0.3, so the numbers are self-consistent and only the Section 5.2 parameter statement was wrong. Re-running at 0.5 would invalidate two pushed commits and re-open the 81-vs-82 boundary episode in order to chase a documentation error.
manuscript_actions: Section 5.2 nominal -> eta_w=0.3, state gust_std=3.0 explicitly
delete the 'independent resampling' explanation of the half-point offset: the offset was caused by the old sweep starting at 0.5, which is 67% stronger than canonical
r_conf for the sweep = 18.932 (v2 calibration); 18.571 was calibrated at 0.5
wind_eta_calibration.root_cause: gust_std existed only as a function default and never appeared in the manuscript, so no reviewer or author could see that eta_w alone does not determine disturbance strength. Disturbance strength is the PRODUCT eta_w * gust_std.

mismatch_wind_rows.note: An earlier claim that MISMATCH.txt held only 8 regimes was a miscount; grep -c '^### ' returns 9. There is no orphan row.

wind_shift_row.ambiguity_warning: This row and the eta=1.0 point of the wind sweep are BOTH labelled 'eta_w=1.0' but differ in two ways: gust_std 5.0 vs 3.0 (strength 5.0 vs 3.0, a 67% difference) and field seed 99 vs 7 (a different realisation). The table row label must disambiguate.

plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.claim: The certificate arms' low bias came from OSQP being used instead of the differentiable QP.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.why_it_appealed: FastCBFMPC does exist and does use OSQP.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.how_it_died: Vanilla passes policy=, and FastCBFMPC is only constructed when policy is None.

plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.claim: The bias was a CPU-vs-CUDA discrepancy.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.why_it_appealed: The arms were re-run on a different device.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.how_it_died: Measured float64 relative error over 20 steps is 1.1e-16, twelve orders of magnitude below the observed 1e-3.

plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.claim: eta_w=0.3 is an alternative normalisation equivalent to the manuscript's 0.5 via gust_std=5.0.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.why_it_appealed: 0.3*5.0 == 0.5*3.0 exactly, and a 'gust 5' does appear in the codebase.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.how_it_died: eval_common.py:116 never passes gust_std; the only gust_std=5.0 lives in the mismatch wind-shift regime. Measured max abs difference 1.356 m/s, ratio exactly 0.6.

plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.claim: The 9th row of tab:mismatch had no provenance and was probably a separate ad-hoc run.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.why_it_appealed: It is the only regime that alters gust_std.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.how_it_died: It sits in the same regimes list at eval_mismatch.py:336; MISMATCH.txt contains 9 '### ' headers, not 8. The premise was a miscount.

plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.claim: The wind sweep covered all six arms.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.why_it_appealed: The log showed no error and every assertion passed.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.how_it_died: wind_sweep_v2.npz held five arms. The Soft-IPP path was wrong and its try/except turned that into a skip. Assertions ran over the arms that existed, so they could not notice the missing one.

plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.claim: A hand-written Newcombe method-10 interval was fit for the binary rows.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.why_it_appealed: Newcombe method 10 is the standard unconditional interval for a paired risk difference, and the formula looked right.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.how_it_died: Two independent checks. It missed Newcombe's own published worked example (n=48, b=12, c=5: computed [-0.2553,-0.0527] against the published [-0.2883,-0.0190], about 70% of the correct width), and it put the delay-2 row (b=5,c=1) entirely below zero while that row's exact McNemar p is 0.22 -- the figure would have claimed a difference the text calls non-significant. The correlation term had been written from memory. Replaced by an exact conditional interval, whose Clopper-Pearson core was first checked against three published values (b=2/m=10, b=0/m=10, b=1/m=20) and matched all three digit for digit.

plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.claim: The 8-point errdir_profile.npz was the plotting data for the RQ5 error profile and merely needed a neutral title plus the Stage-1b curve.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.why_it_appealed: The file sat in fig_data next to the audited v2 products, was loaded by a figure script that named it the preferred source, and had one array per arm with exactly the three arm names used by the table.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.how_it_died: Arithmetic, before any plotting. Stage-1b's buckets span 1.82-2.14 m but the table reports a critical error of 1.04 m, and no subset of numbers all above 1.8 can average to 1.04. Reading the producer then exposed three geometric deviations, and the file turned out to define no abscissa at all. Recomputation from the authoritative geometry hit the table to 5e-3 on all six values.

plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.claim: A single focused ordinate of [-2.2,+2.2] m would serve both panels of Fig. 9, since the only extreme value is encounter 93's arm-level e_parallel.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.why_it_appealed: Encounter 93 is the sole |e_par| > 8 m case and its paired difference is a mild +1.299 m, so the difference axis looked comfortably inside the same range as the arm axis.
plausible_but_falsified_diagnoses.how_it_died: A clipping assertion on the difference panel. The paired differences run from -2.289 to +2.399 m, so six points sat outside the shared range and matplotlib was dropping them without complaint. Panel (b) was widened to [-2.6,+2.6] and the assertion now fails on any clipped point. The lesson is that 'the outlier is handled' does not imply 'the derived quantity fits the same axis'.

lessons.rule: An arithmetic coincidence is a hypothesis about the code, not evidence about it. Read the call site, then measure. Three of the four diagnoses above were arithmetically or structurally attractive and all were killed by one grep or one measurement.
lessons.rule_2: Never wrap data production in try/except. A wrong path must crash, not degrade into absent data: no assertion can fire on a record that was never written.
lessons.rule_3: Before plotting any computed interval, check the implementation against a published worked example AND against an independent order-of-magnitude estimate. This defect was caught because a rough estimate of about +/-2.4 pp had been stated in advance and the implementation disagreed with it; that cross-check cost minutes, whereas a post-hoc audit of a published figure would not.
lessons.rule_4: A data file is not provenance. Before plotting an archived array, verify it reduces to an already-published number by an explicit weighted identity, and confirm its abscissa is defined somewhere. errdir_profile.npz passed every superficial test - right directory, right arm names, right shape, a script that called it authoritative - and was still computed with a different CPA anchor, a different frame, a one-step time offset and a different episode horizon.
lessons.rule_5: The log-ordinate veto is conditioned on zero-reference semantics, not on dynamic range. It was issued for Fig. 5, whose entire claim rests on a zero line (the rescue threshold) that a log axis cannot represent. An error profile carries no such reference, so the veto does not reach it. Fig. 8 still avoids a log ordinate for an independent reason: its comparison of record is multiplicative (1.04 against 4.07 m critical error), and a log axis renders a factor of four as a constant visual offset, hiding the very gap the figure exists to show. Two stacked linear panels at their own full ranges were used instead. Cite this rather than re-litigating when cross-range data recurs.
lessons.rule_6: Verify overlay placement geometrically, not by pixel colour. A colour-counting check on Fig. 8 reported all three arms as colliding with the legends when none did: the curves span the full panel width, so colour cannot distinguish 'curve beneath the legend' from 'curve elsewhere in the same pixel rows'. The reliable test compares each overlay's window extent against the curves' display-coordinate vertices AND the densely sampled segments between them, which names the offending segment instead of returning a pixel count. It caught two real collisions the pixel method had buried in false positives. Note also that an inset's tight bounding box extends about 0.056 of the host panel's height below its axes frame once a y-label and tick text are present, so a gap sized against the axes frame alone is not enough.
lessons.rule_7: Assert that no axis clips its data. Two separate defects in this figure set were invisible without it: Fig. 9's difference panel silently dropped six of 200 points that lay outside a range chosen for the arm panel, and the left margin clipped nothing but antialiasing. Range choices made for one panel do not transfer to a panel showing a derived quantity, so check each axis against min and max of what it actually draws, and check the canvas edges for ink after rendering.

wind_sweep_v2.strength_note: Disturbance strength is eta_w * gust_std. The grid spans 0.9 to 4.5, i.e. exactly five times the canonical 0.9. The canonical 0.3 point was ADDED to the grid so the sweep and the main table share an operating point.

zero_effect_bounds.reading: Across a five-fold increase in disturbance strength no arm moves by more than 1.5 pp in conflict rate (3 of 200 episodes) or 0.049 m in mean minimum separation. This is sampling noise at n=200, not a dose response, which is why the sweep is reported as a sentence and given no figure panel: drawing a zero effect as a trend line invites a slope that is not there.

wind_sweep_v2.canonical_point_assertion: wind_sweep(eta=0.3) conflict vectors are ELEMENTWISE identical to conflict_vectors_v2 for all four common-planner arms. This replaces the manuscript's earlier explanation of a half-point offset as 'independent resampling': the offset was caused by the old sweep starting at eta=0.5, a 67% stronger field, and with the canonical point in the grid there is no offset left to explain.
wind_sweep_v2.soft_ipp_backfill: The first sweep ran five arms, not six. Soft-IPP was constructed inside a try/except pointing at {PLANGRAD_DIR}/soft_joint.pt, but that checkpoint lives in code/baselines/04_soft_ipp/. The except branch logged a warning and dropped the arm, so a wrong path degraded into a silently missing arm -- a self-check cannot fire on data that was never produced. Backfilled by patch_softipp_wind.py, which appends only and then re-verifies that all 62 pre-existing arrays are byte-identical. Its eta=0.3 point reproduces Table 1 (CR 53.0, Energy 16.975).

matched_pair_v2.max_lateral_offset_provenance: Produced by importing p2_mcnemar_dev.rollout, the byte-identical function that wrote DEV_MATCHED_S1B.txt, rather than re-implementing the cross-track geometry inside evaluate_policy (which would have been a third rollout implementation). Audited: the weights in Round1/04_weights have the same md5 as the plangrad weights dir; the cached arrays give S1b 103.0183 +/- 16.8405 and S2 103.5336 +/- 11.2749, matching the txt's 103.02 +/- 16.84 and 103.53 +/- 11.27; ETA_W=0.3, wind seed 7, encounter seed 12345, pool 2500-3000.
matched_pair_v2.critical_value_discipline: The two source txts used DIFFERENT critical values and both must be honoured to reproduce them: EFF_MATCHED_S1B.txt used Student-t (t_crit(0.975,199)=1.972), DEV_MATCHED_S1B.txt reused p2_mcnemar_dev.paired_diff_ci with z=1.96. tab:stage1b's min-sep interval is the t interval (z would give [-0.3473,+0.2653], not the published [-0.35,+0.27]).
matched_pair_v2.binary_interval_method: Exact conditional interval for the paired risk difference: condition on the m=b+c discordant pairs, place a Clopper-Pearson interval on theta=b/m, and map through d=(1-2*theta)*m/n, a monotone linear map that carries the endpoints. Chosen over Newcombe's method 10 because the manuscript reports these five comparisons with exact McNemar tests and an unconditional approximation is not guaranteed to agree with a conditional test.
matched_pair_v2.consistency_assertion: Every interval spans zero if and only if the exact McNemar p exceeds 0.05. All five rows span zero (p = 1.00, 1.00, 1.00, 0.22, 0.50), as do all three continuous rows: 0 of 8 exclude zero.
matched_pair_v2.boundary_note: At b=m (the combined row, (2,0)) the Clopper-Pearson upper limit for theta is exactly 1, so the lower endpoint of d coincides with the point estimate. Correct exact-interval behaviour at the boundary, not a defect.
matched_pair_v2.scope: Closed-loop operational metrics only. ADE and critical-window error are prediction-space quantities and belong to Table 1 and tab:errdir; the exclusion is by quantity type, not by outcome.

errdir_v2.purpose: Fig. 8 (CPA error profile) and Fig. 9 (task-aligned fingerprint). Replaces errdir_profile.npz, which is deprecated; see deprecates_errdir_profile below.

contents.profile__<arm>: mean |prediction error| per |k - k_CPA| bucket, k = 0..7, metres
contents.counts__<arm>: contributing steps per bucket: 200 at k=0 (one CPA step per episode), 400 for the symmetric pairs, 396/389/380 at k=5/6/7 from horizon truncation
contents.epi_par__<arm>: per-episode critical-window mean e_parallel, n=200, metres, negative = neighbour predicted closer to the ego than it truly is

errdir_v2.geometry_provenance: Recomputed with the geometry of diag_error_direction.measure() and p0_errdir_episode.per_episode(), the functions that wrote RQ5_PROFILE.txt and P0_ERRDIR_EPISODE.txt. The prediction is carried to the absolute frame (pred_abs = mean_pred*SCALE + nei_origin) and compared against nf[:,0,1:h+1,:], the CPA step is taken from the ego REFERENCE trajectory ref[:,1:h+1,:], and episodes are sampled at T = T_EPISODE = 20.
errdir_v2.binding_self_check: The profile is bound to tab:rq5-profile by construction rather than by inspection: the step-count-weighted mean of buckets 0-3 must equal each arm's tabulated critical error to 5e-3 (achieved 13.5350 / 1.0390 / 4.0678 against 13.53 / 1.04 / 4.07) and the complement must equal the inert value (23.1369 / 2.0822 / 4.3983 against 23.14 / 2.08 / 4.40). Episode-level means, SEMs and toward-ego fractions reproduce P0_ERRDIR_EPISODE.txt to 5e-4, and the paired S2-S1b contrast reproduces -0.1639 m with paired-t p=0.007399 and Wilcoxon p=0.001137; its t-interval is [-0.2833,-0.0445] against the manuscript's [-0.283,-0.045]. The script refuses to write the npz if any of these fails.
errdir_v2.deprecates_errdir_profile: errdir_profile.npz (from collect_fig_data.py::errdir_profile) is DEPRECATED and must not be plotted. It could not reproduce tab:rq5-profile by any subsetting: its Stage-1b buckets spanned 1.82-2.14 m while the table's critical value is 1.04 m, so no subset of larger numbers can average to a smaller one. Three substantive deviations from the authoritative geometry were found. (1) It anchored the CPA on the ego's INITIAL position x0[:,0:3], a fixed point, instead of the moving ego reference trajectory, so the same physical step landed in a different bucket. (2) It differenced in the recentred/scaled space and multiplied by SCALE, indexing nfut[:,0,:h], instead of comparing absolute-frame positions against nf[:,0,1:h+1,:] - a one-step time offset against a different array. (3) It sampled T=30 rather than T_EPISODE=20, which changes the reference trajectory and hence the CPA step. The file also carried no definition of its own abscissa.
errdir_v2.stage2_spike_resolved: The deprecated file showed an isolated Stage-2 value of 12.638 at bucket 1 between neighbours of 2.424 and 3.294. Under the authoritative geometry the spike does not exist: the Stage-2 profile is 3.733 3.931 4.127 4.313 4.713 4.600 5.327 4.649, with no bucket above three times its median. The spike was an artefact of the deprecated CPA anchoring, not a physical feature, so it is not mentioned in the caption.
errdir_v2.profile_shapes: Outer-to-inner ratio (bucket 7 / bucket 0) quantifies the three shapes: Stage 1 flat at 1.056 (a predictor that never saw the encounter distribution has no CPA structure), Stage-1b mildly rising at 1.163 while lowest everywhere, Stage 2 rising at 1.245. This is the graphical form of the critical/inert ratios 0.585 / 0.499 / 0.925. Note the two quantities use different denominators: the profile stops at bucket 7, whereas the inert value aggregates every step beyond the critical window, which is why Stage 1's inert 23.14 m exceeds the profile's right-hand end of 14.32 m.

fig09_fingerprint.purpose: Fig. 9, the task-aligned error fingerprint. Gardner-Altman estimation plot of the paired Stage-2 minus Stage-1b contrast in episode-mean e_parallel.
fig09_fingerprint.why_gardner_altman: The quantity of record is a paired contrast on the same 200 encounters, so the difference and its interval belong on their own axis aligned with the arm-level data. A histogram would discard the pairing and a raincloud would show two marginal distributions whose overlap says nothing about the within-encounter difference.
fig09_fingerprint.interval: Panel (b) draws a percentile bootstrap interval, 20000 resamples, numpy default_rng(12345): [-0.2799,-0.0464] m. The Student-t interval [-0.2833,-0.0445] is reproduced as a self-check against the manuscript's [-0.283,-0.045] and the two agree to about 3 mm, so the choice of interval does not carry the conclusion.
fig09_fingerprint.encounter_93: A lone geometric extreme: Stage-1 -54.086, Stage-1b -47.520, Stage-2 -46.220 m, against a second-largest Stage-1b magnitude of -1.079 m. All three arms are extreme together, so the encounter geometry is anomalous rather than any predictor. It is the only encounter with |e_par| > 8 m in either arm, and its paired difference (+1.299 m) is unremarkable, which is the paired design doing its job.
fig09_fingerprint.outlier_rendering: Panel (a) focuses on [-2.2,+2.2] m and marks encounter 93 at the axis edge with arrows and its numeric values, rather than clipping it silently or letting it compress the other 199 encounters into a line. This is annotation off-scale, not a broken axis: nothing is hidden and the encounter's paired difference is drawn normally in panel (b), circled and labelled. Panel (b) spans [-2.6,+2.6] because its data reach -2.289 and +2.399 m and no outlier justifies clipping there; the two panels therefore carry different ordinate ranges, which the caption states. A self-check refuses to plot if either panel would clip a point.
fig09_fingerprint.leave_one_out: Dropping encounter 93 moves the paired mean from -0.1639 to -0.1712 m and the paired-t p from 0.00740 to 0.00507, so the contrast is robust to it. The ARM-level dispersion is not: Stage-1b goes from -0.176 +/- 0.239 to +0.062 +/- 0.025 (the sign of the mean flips and the SEM falls by a factor of 9.5) and Stage-2 from -0.340 +/- 0.235 to -0.109 +/- 0.047. tab:errdir's SEMs and its '|mean| > 2 SEM ? NO' verdict are therefore driven by this single encounter. The n=200 figures remain the reported ones, but a leave-one-out footnote states this so a referee's sensitivity analysis finds nothing unannounced.
fig09_fingerprint.geometry_inset: A small inset in panel (a) fixes the sign convention with five elements only: ego, true neighbour, predicted neighbour, the line-of-sight axis, and the projection labelled e_parallel < 0. It is an extension of the axis label rather than a concept schematic, which is why it is an inset and not a panel. Placed in the empty upper band: measured occupancy shows no point and no connecting line reaches [+1.8,+2.2] m, and the Stage-1b column is empty above +0.959 m.
